description: q (natesales/q): small command-line DNS client with support for UDP, TCP, DNS-over-TLS, DNS-over-HTTPS (HTTP/2 and HTTP/3), DNS-over-QUIC, Oblivious DoH and DNSCrypt. Installed as the command qdns.
notes: Command: qdns (not q: main/q is an unrelated tool that runs SQL on CSV files and also adds the q command).
The 'q (DNS client)' shortcut in Scoop Apps shows examples and waits for a key.
Without @server, q on Windows does NOT use your network's DNS: it looks for /etc/resolv.conf, finds none and
queries Cloudflare over DNS-over-HTTPS. To ask the router, give its address: qdns example.com @192.168.1.1
Or set a default: SET Q_DEFAULT_SERVER=9.9.9.9 (cmd) or $env:Q_DEFAULT_SERVER = '9.9.9.9' (PowerShell).

script: # q.exe prints its help and exits at once, so the 'q (DNS client)' shortcut opens this micro-launcher instead.
':: q (DNS client): shows what qdns does and how to run it, then waits for a key.',
':: Written by the gesu Scoop bucket at install time.',
'ECHO q is a command-line DNS client. This package installs it as qdns:',
'ECHO the q command belongs to an unrelated tool (main/q, SQL on CSV files).',
'ECHO Without @server qdns asks Cloudflare over DNS-over-HTTPS, not your network.',
'ECHO Set Q_DEFAULT_SERVER to change that, for example: SET Q_DEFAULT_SERVER=192.168.1.1',
'ECHO       A, AAAA, NS, MX, TXT and CNAME records at once',
'ECHO       Chosen types from Quad9 over plain DNS',
'ECHO       Output like dig; also json, yaml, column',
